description: NYCSim material name -> CC0 PBR texture source. Every asset id was checked against the provider API and its preview inspected visually by the facade-kit agent (2026-09-05). physical_size_m = real-world metres covered by one texture tile (Poly Haven publishes it; AmbientCG values are measured from the downloaded colour map with size_rule by `python3 blender/common/textures.py --measure`: brick_course = 67.5 mm NYC/modular course, lap = 101.6 mm vinyl double-4 exposure, plank = 140 mm cedar stave, tile = 100 mm, corrugation = 68 mm (2 2/3 in) pitch). tint multiplies the colour map; color_override replaces it (paint colours); roughness_override / roughness_scale adjust the roughness map. provider 'procedural' entries return {} from get_texture_set and carry their shader parameters in `procedural`. `breakup` bakes a seamless low-frequency luminance variation (soot, rain-streaking, patched brick) into the kit's 1K colour map for wall-scale materials, so the tile repeat stops reading as wallpaper across a facade; it is baked into the image, so it survives the glTF export.
license: All entries CC0 1.0 (AmbientCG: Lennart Demes / ambientCG; Poly Haven: authors recorded in LICENSE.json on download).

red_brick.notes: weathered red common brick, light mortar; Old Law tenements, lofts, rowhouses

red_brick_orange.notes: cleaner orange-red face brick; 1920s–50s apartments, schools

brown_brick.notes: medium brown face brick; 1960s–80s apartment / office

dark_brick.notes: dark grey-black brick; 1980s condos, modern infill

tan_brick.notes: buff / tan brick; New Law tenements, 1920s setback offices, Art Deco

white_glazed_brick.notes: white glazed brick, grey mortar; 1955–75 UES apartment towers

brownstone.notes: joint-free brown sandstone for monolithic trim: stoops, lintels, sills, quoins, cornice blocks (Portland brownstone tone via tint)

brownstone_ashlar.notes: dark red-brown sandstone ashlar with joints for whole brownstone facades (shell shader)

limestone.notes: joint-free cream limestone for trim: lintels, sills, string courses, bank columns, cornices (Indiana limestone tone)

limestone_ashlar.notes: light ashlar blocks with joints for limestone bases and bank facades (shell shader)

terracotta.notes: glazed cream architectural terracotta (Flatiron / Woolworth buff); joint-free for moulded ornament

cast_iron.notes: painted grey cast iron (SoHo storefront columns, areaway railings); apply tint for cream/white/green painted fronts

glass_curtain.notes: tinted reflective vision/spandrel glass for curtain-wall modules; texture-free (mullions are geometry)

glass_clear.notes: clear window / storefront plate glass: near-black diffuse with a 4 % Fresnel specular and 26 % alpha over the interior room box. Glass has essentially no diffuse albedo — giving it one is what made the first pass read as flat grey plastic in full sun. Roughness is 0.09 rather than mirror-smooth: a razor-sharp lobe on a small pane is a firefly source, and real float glass in an old sash is never optically flat.

concrete.notes: cast-in-place concrete with board/form marks; parking garages, NYCHA slab edges, bulkheads

precast.notes: smooth light precast / cast stone; sills, copings, panels

concrete_sidewalk.notes: weathered grey broom-finish concrete; sidewalk flags (joints are geometry / shader), stoop landings

stucco.notes: white rough stucco; Tudor gables, Mediterranean houses, EIFS sign bands

vinyl_siding.notes: clean cream lap siding read as vinyl double-4 (101.6 mm exposure); Queens / Staten Island houses

wood_clapboard.notes: weathered painted wood clapboard; frame rowhouses

stone_rubble.notes: grey-tan rubble ashlar (Manhattan schist / fieldstone) for churches and mansions

metal_panel.notes: satin light-grey aluminium / insulated metal panel; hospitals, self-storage, modern infill

granite.notes: light grey speckled granite, honed; bank bases, lobby floors, curbs

granite_rusticated.notes: rock-faced granite blocks for rusticated bases and retaining walls

tar_roof.notes: flaking aluminium-coated tar roof over black asphalt; tenement roofs

tar_gravel_roof.notes: built-up tar and gravel roof; lofts, schools

corrugated_metal.notes: bare galvanised corrugated steel; sheds, fences, elevated station houses

painted_metal_green.notes: hunter-green painted steel (fire escapes, lamp posts, sidewalk-shed frames); colour is linear sRGB #2C4B38, roughness/normal from the scuffed-steel map

painted_metal_black.notes: matte black painted metal with drips; fire escapes, railings, roll gates, window guards

rust.notes: dark rusted steel; water-tower dunnage, old fire-escape ladders, roof hatches

cedar_wood.notes: weathered grey-brown cedar boards with nail rows; water-tower staves (UV rotated vertical)

painted_wood_white.notes: cream painted wood; window sash, dormers, trim

plywood_green.notes: weathered green painted plywood; NYC sidewalk-shed parapet and construction fence. tint takes the painted-wood map down to hunter green (sRGB ~ #26523A) while keeping the plank grain.

steel_galvanized.notes: galvanised spangle steel; scaffold pipe, RTU housings, ducts

aluminum_anodized.notes: clear anodised aluminium; window frames, sliders, storefront frames, AC units

bronze_anodized.notes: dark bronze anodised aluminium; 1970s curtain-wall mullions, 1980s condo windows

interior_tile.notes: white 100 mm ceramic tile; bodega / laundromat / pharmacy walls and floors

subway_tile.notes: white 3x6 subway tile; deli, pizza, bar walls

interior_wood_floor.notes: oak strip floor; clothing store, bar, residential lobby

tyre_rubber.notes: tyre rubber; the tread and sidewall of every vehicle in the city. 0.25 m covers one texture tile, which puts the grain at the scale of a real tread block on a 205/55R16

leather_seat.notes: black upholstery leather; car seats and door cards

seat_cloth.notes: woven seat cloth; the trim level most of the fleet has

carpet_automotive.notes: cut-pile carpet; vehicle floor and boot lining

metal_brushed.notes: brushed stainless; interior trim, door sills, pedal faces
